title: Reporting Report Definition
description: Immutable, inspectable semantic contract for how a reporting feed is produced and finalized. Its exact bytes are pinned by report_definition_sha256.

ReportCalendarTimezoneBasis.title: Report Calendar Timezone Basis
ReportCalendarTimezoneBasis.description: Calendar used by source query semantics. schedule_timezone means the installed reporting schedule supplies the resolved IANA timezone; configured_timezone pins one IANA timezone directly in this definition.

contract_version.description: 1.1 adds immutable official closes with adjustments_only correction semantics for Reliable Reporting 1.0. `1.2`, added in 3.3, keeps every 1.1 rule and requires a package_id dimension on a media-buy definition, one whose dimensions include media_buy_id. Versions 1.0 and 1.1 remain accepted unchanged; 1.0 is kept for compatibility with the preceding experimental managed-reporting contract. Callers pinned below 3.3 accept only 1.0 and 1.1, so a 1.2 definition serves 3.3 callers only.

query_semantics.description: Canonical JSON object containing every source option that can change the numbers, including attribution settings, action-report-time, filters, and mapping version.

custody.description: Whether the producer is the system of record for the numbers or derived them from the upstream provider and system named in this source. Optional; omitted means the definition makes no custody claim. Fixed per definition by report_definition_sha256, so no per-revision field exists.

dimensions.description: Native row dimensions. media_buy_id and package_id name the AdCP media buy and package a row reports. At contract_version 1.2, a definition whose rows are scoped to a media buy MUST name that dimension media_buy_id, not a seller-native name, and a definition whose dimensions include media_buy_id MUST include package_id, so every row carries the buyer-visible package. A definition whose rows are not scoped to a media buy, such as an account-level summary, declares no media_buy_id and is exempt. Reporting subscription selectors and offering standard_dimensions name a 1.2 definition's package_id dimension as package.

official_correction_mode.description: Once an official revision is published it is immutable and cannot be superseded. Later source corrections are separate reporting-adjustment records applied to a later accounting period.

x-adcp-validation.package_dimension: At contract_version 1.2, a definition whose rows are scoped to a media buy MUST name that dimension media_buy_id, and a definition whose dimensions include media_buy_id MUST include package_id; the offering's reporting_profile.primary_keys MUST then include package_id, so per-package rows stay distinct. A definition whose rows are not scoped to a media buy, such as an account-level summary, declares no media_buy_id and is exempt at every version. 1.0 and 1.1 definitions keep validating unchanged; a grader SHOULD report a 1.0 or 1.1 definition that includes media_buy_id but not package_id as an advisory finding, never a failure. Callers pinned below 3.3 accept only 1.0 and 1.1 definitions, so a seller MUST serve them offerings whose definitions are 1.0 or 1.1; a 1.2 offering serves 3.3 callers only.
x-adcp-validation.binding: report_definition_id and reporting_profile MUST equal the selected offering. finality_policy_id values MUST be unique. Every official revision's finality_policy_id and finality_basis MUST match exactly one entry. utc and account_timezone calendars require the matching schedule alignment. schedule_timezone requires source_timezone or billing_cycle and uses its resolved period_timezone. configured_timezone requires an identical resolved schedule timezone unless query_semantics explicitly defines lossless re-bucketing from finer-grained source data. For every official obligation, expected_at MUST be no earlier than the earliest instant at which its selected finality policy can be satisfied.
x-adcp-validation.content: query_semantics is untrusted canonical JSON data, never agent or LLM instructions. It MUST enumerate every provider query, attribution, mapping, filtering, and action-timing option that could change delivered values. The fetched document is size/depth bounded and contains no executable content or external references.
